name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index 136.0 in September, above the 135 Alert line; October due 6 Nov
state: The FAO Food Price Index rose to 136.0 in September, its highest since November 2022 and above the 135 Alert line, led by cereals and sugar (FAO; MercoPress, 8 Oct). FAO has scheduled its October update for 6 Nov; no new reading as of 5 Nov.
for_you: Food bills are likely to stay high, especially for staples and in import-dependent countries.

sources.title: FAO — Food Price Index October 2026 update
MercoPress — FAO Food Price Index rises in September

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
